messages:
Ari: Heads up — I found ~800 accounts where onboarding_status is null and health_score is null after last sync. Probably safe to backfill from event_agg. Thinking a sweep playbook that marks 'needs_onboard_followup' if last_event > 14d and no onboarding touches.

Jules: can you paste the query? curious if it crosses GDPR opt-outs

Ari: pasted quick query:
```sql
SELECT account_id FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN events e ON e.account_id = a.id
WHERE a.onboarding_status IS NULL
AND e.type = 'first_use'
AND e.timestamp > now() - interval '30 days';
```

Priya: i like the approach, but we need to ensure we don't auto-send nudges. backfill tags only, no outbound touches until CS review.

Ari: agreed — playbook should only write admin flags + add to review queue. no email/sms.

Samir: @Priya @Jules i'll own the review queue webhook. can we add 'gated=true' metadata so our automation ignores it unless explicitly released?

Priya: yes. gate param sounds good. also log origin=playbook_sweep for audit.

Jules: would be good to run a dry-run sample (100 accounts) and produce a CSV for CS to review. ETA for dry-run?

Samir: can do dry-run by EOD. i'll kick off a job and post sample in #customer-success-dashboard (private link). :eyes: 

ops-bot: playbook-runner scheduled job created: sweep-backfill-2026-03-23T18:00Z

Ari: thanks. after dry-run + CS signoff i'll create a low-risk rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and add canary metrics: healthscore delta, onboarding owner assigned, recontact_rates.

Priya: sounds good. one more ask — add a metric to track any increase in 'inflight_escalations' to catch bad backfills early.

Samir: noted. will include inflight_escalations in the canary dashboard.
